extraction_note: No source checked out on disk â€” extracted compiled Next.js server output (.next/server/) from the lobehub/lobe-chat:latest image via docker create + targeted docker cp of specific compiled route files (full /app copy aborted on node_modules symlinks, same as other Node-based images on this Windows host), then read middleware.js and the chat route.js directly.
notes: PARTIALLY VERIFIED â€” recording what was and wasn't confirmed rather than guessing on the unresolved part. Real inference route confirmed via compiled route tree: /app/.next/server/app/(backend)/webapi/chat/[provider]/route.js (also a hardcoded /webapi/chat/azureai/route.js variant) â€” App Router middleware-manifest.json confirms /(api|trpc|webapi)(.*) is matched by src/middleware.js. Middleware.js parses `process.env.ACCESS_CODE?.split(',').filter(Boolean)||[]` into an ACCESS_CODES config value; this target's docker-compose.yml sets ACCESS_CODE='' (empty string), which parses to an empty array. The chat route.js itself references and calls a `checkAuth` function, confirming SOME auth gate exists in the real code path (this is not an ungated/dead-code route) â€” but the checkAuth implementation itself is imported from a separate compiled chunk not extracted in this pass, so I could NOT trace whether an empty ACCESS_CODES array means the gate opens (no code required) or falls back to a different auth mode (e.g. required OAuth login). Recording ai_auth_gated as null/not-verified rather than asserting either way â€” LobeChat's publicly documented behavior is that an empty ACCESS_CODE disables the access-code prompt, but that is product documentation, not something I confirmed by reading the checkAuth logic itself in this build, and the project standard here is to not assert from documentation what wasn't verified in code. soft_404_behavior verified via presence of Next.js's standard _not-found route artifacts (app/_not-found.html/.rsc/.meta) â€” standalone Next servers return a real 404 status for unmatched app-router paths, not a SPA index.html fallback (contrast with the Express/FastAPI SPA-style catch-alls seen in flowise/anythingllm/open-webui).
